E2752024715.title: About
E2752024715.content:
Profile

Hélio Teles (b. 1982, Lisbon) is a Montreal-based multidisciplinary designer bridging strategy and design.


With over 15 years of international experience, he has collaborated with studios and clients alike to define, transform, and launch brands across industries such as technology, food and beverage, culture, and education.

Hélio brings a proven ability to drive, create, and present graphic design concepts both independently and as part of a team. His work consistently blends strategic thinking with strong visual execution to deliver foundational and lasting design solutions.

Throughout his career, he has managed design teams, mentored emerging talent, led client workshops and presentations, and developed comprehensive design strategies and visual directions. His practice is grounded in a thoughtful approach to branding, visual identity, and cross-disciplinary collaboration.

All work by Hélio Teles — including self-initiated, freelance, and in-studio projects created in collaboration with teams at Bruce Mau Design, Goods & Services, Whitman Emorson, Rice Studios, Principal and Two Times Elliott.

Z4223404401.title: Union
Z4223404401.content:
001

UNION
Visual Identity

Two Times Elliott
2025















Brand identity for UNION, a managed office services provider shaping a new hybrid workplace model that blends the flexibility of co-working with the stability of traditional leasing. Pioneers of this approach in the UK, UNION offers a seamless, end-to-end experience for companies seeking dedicated, high-quality workspaces. The identity repositions UNION within a crowded and emerging sector by elevating service into experience. Inspired by the unseen systems and relationships behind the managed office model, the visual language emphasizes clarity, cohesion, and unification—positioning UNION as a confident, category-leading partner for today’s most influential companies.

Creative Directors: James Horwitz & Edmund Lock
Strategist: Mark Pavitt
Senior Designer: Hélio Teles
Project Manager: Lovisa Molund

P2411706481.title: PéA
P2411706481.content:
002

Première équipe Architecture
Visual Identity

Principal
2024















Brand identity for PéA, an architecture studio specialized in sports facilities and community spaces. Since 1985, Poirier Fontaine Architectes has been distinguished as a key player in the design of sports and aquatic facilities in Quebec. To celebrate its 45th anniversary, the firm crafted a new vision, focused on the commitment to address contemporary challenges in architecture, with a focus on sustainability, energy efficiency and resilience to climate change. The new identity captures the very essence of this transformation. The visual system celebrates the relationship between sports and community, positioning PéA as a creator of living places, where each space promotes and nourishes common well-being.

Creative Director: Bryan-K. Lamonde
Senior Designer: Hélio Teles
Designer: Émile Painchaud
Project Manager: Justine Crépeau-Viau

P3102465491.title: Plural
P3102465491.content:
003

Plural 2024
Campaign

Principal
2024















Campaign for Plural, Montreal’s largest contemporary art fair. Formerly known as Papier, Montreal's largest contemporary art fair has undergone a major transformation, giving birth to Plural. The fair now celebrates a wide diversity of artistic mediums, from paper to sculpture, digital art to installations.The new identity is modulated to the rhythm of playful yet minimalist typographic compositions, keeping the spotlight on the artworks while echoing the festive character of the fair.

Creative Director: Bryan-K. Lamonde
Senior Designer: Hélio Teles
Visual Identity: Julien Hébert & Mali Savaria-Ille
Project Manager: Justine Crépeau-Viau & Chloé Miglierina

V0743474759.title: Orio
V0743474759.content:
004

Orio Cloud
Visual Identity

Principal
2024















Orio is a cloud storage and network connectivity provider for creative industries. Based in Québec, Orio operates a decentralized network of data centres, that use the energy of its servers to heat buildings. The aim is to reduce carbon footprint and promote a sustainable future. Inspired by constellation Orion, the brand name is the main driver of the new identity and embodies the company’s core values and services.

Creative Director: Bryan-K. Lamonde
Senior Designer: Hélio Teles
Project Manager: Justine Crépeau-Viau

O2772845937.title: Graver l'homme
O2772845937.content:
005

Graver l’homme
Title Sequence

Principal
2024















“Graver l’homme” guides us through the inspiring and poetic labyrinth that is the life and work of Pierre Hébert. Since the 1960s, celebrated animator Pierre Hébert has experimented with the full gamut of styles, from abstract animation to more narrative approaches, as well as collage, drawing and live performance. Employing an arresting black-and-white palette punctuated with animated flourishes, Scratches of Life: The Art of Pierre Hébert unwinds the thread of the scratch-on-film technique, guiding us through the inspiring labyrinth of Hébert’s life and work. The intimate, creative approach pays homage to his protean oeuvre, fusing his human and artistic journeys into one. Director Loïc Darses in turn relies on novel imagemaking concepts to capture the imprint of an extraordinary artist who, to this day and even while battling illness, continues to create, striving to share his vision of new forms of life.

Creative Director: Bryan-K. Lamonde
Senior Designer: Hélio Teles
Project Managers: Justine Crépeau-Viau & Chloé Miglierina

K0693362822.title: Rice Talks
K0693362822.content:
006

Rice Talks
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2023















Rice Talks is a studio initiative with the purpose of sharing experiences and innovative thinking from brands and individuals. On the occasion of its 10th anniversary, rice launched "rice talks”—a platform for thought leaders and change-makers to engage with the wider community, showcasing the incredible work being done across various industries, particularly in Vietnam. The first edition took place in early 2023 under the theme Sustainability in Design and featured, Pizza 4P’s, PlasticPeople and Repeet. The solution is a type-driven visual identity system that supports the studio’s manifesto of amplify voices and broadcast extraordinary stories.

Creative Director: Joshua Breidenbach
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Designer: Lim Nuel

Y2878134490.title: Laha Coffee
Y2878134490.content:
007

Laha Coffee
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2023















Laha is a Vietnamese producer of agricultural products, specialized in coffee, with retail stores across Vietnam. The company’s mission is to make organic products commonplace in Vietnam, by supporting local farmers implementing sustainable farming practices, to explore the full potential of Vietnamese products. The design reflects the brand’s commitment to organic farming standards, sustainable practices, and community support. The new identity is an evolution from the previous coffee bean logotype and introduces the sprout, signifying development and long-term growth.

Creative Director: Joshua Breidenbach
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Senior Designer: Tien Nguyen
Designers: Hieu Vo & Lim Nuel
Project Manager: Thao My Nguyen

Z1029117610.title: Eastlake
Z1029117610.content:
008

Eastlake
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2022















Visual identity and packaging system for Eastlake, a brewery and taproom in Minneapolis. The scope of work was to evolve the old brand and create a clear identity and packaging system. The solution focuses on the unique and distinct character of Eastlake’s staple beers, Kirby Pucker, Southside, Dank Aaron and Sundogs’. The design draws inspiration from B-movie titles and puts the beers on the centre stage of the brand.

Creative Director: Joshua Breidenbach
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Senior Designer: Tien Nguyen
Lettering: Duc Cao
Project Manager: Ha Anh H.

X3239372680.title: Repeet
X3239372680.content:
009

Repeet
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2022















Repeet is a Vietnamese textile brand specialized in alternative material solutions for the fashion industry. Driven by the vision of creating a future where fashion has a positive impact on the environment, Repeet transforms plastic waste into textiles, throughout a network of partnerships—from waste collection to transformation—promoting a circular economy that benefits the community. The name takes inspiration from Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and “repeat” to create a brand that is actionable and instantly recognizable.

Creative Director: Joshua Breidenbach
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Senior Designer: Tien Nguyen
Project Manager: Ha Anh H.

Y1715500216.title: Keos
Y1715500216.content:
010

Keos
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2021















Visual identity and packaging system for a new player in the pet food industry. Keos is a French-Vietnamese pet food brand established in 2021. Drawing inspiration from the straightforward & raw aesthetics of popular DIY movements, such as punk rock, the visual direction achieves a bold sense of passion and uniqueness while remaining functional & approachable.

Creative Director: Gregory Jewett
Design Director: Hélio Teles

Project Manager: Ha Anh H.

W2986420693.title: Hoang Long Minerals
W2986420693.content:
011

Hoāng Long Minerals
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2021















Defining a brand platform for conscious mining in balance with nature. With 10 years experience in the mining industry in Vietnam, Hoāng Long was looking to define a clear brand platform and to create a brand that fully embodies its scope and impact in the community. The design solution celebrates the company’s achievements, while keeping in mind the impact it has on the environment and the surrounding communities. Under the motto of “Keeping the Balance”, the brand identity expresses growth and the responsibility to maintain a perfect balance between business and nature.

Creative Directors: Joshua Breidenbach & Sebastiaan Weyler
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Designers: Hieu Vo, Nu Nguyen, Lan Lê,  Lim Nuel & Parker Metcalf
Project Managers: Y-Van Pham & Ha Anh H.

X1397010600.title: The Sangomas
X1397010600.content:
013

The Sangomas
Record Cover

Freelance
2021















Art direction for The Sangomas’ closing act “Nowhere Ain’t Too Far From Here”. Somewhat like a sleazy sucker punch in a sordid late-night dive, these roarin' rock 'n' rollers dish out a paralyzing blow to the brain. Spawned from Montreal's dirty snow-sludge-ridden sewers, The Sangomas churn riffs straight outta the mid 70s to a boisterous beat of frustrated felony.  

Design: Hélio Teles
Video: Marie-Espérance Cerdà

C2892346605.title: Coexist Or Die
C2892346605.content:
015

Coexist Or Die
Poster

Rice Studios
2020















Coexist—to live or exist together, in peace, at the same time, or in the same place. In the summer of 2020 Slanted initiated a global call for submissions questioning topics such as climate change, political power, human rights, freedom of speech, wars, and many other global issues. More than 450 designers, illustrators, photographers, writers and artists from all over the world contributed to this extra thick issue (almost 100 pages extra—352 instead of 256). Coexist Or Die focus on the urgency of the now and places the viewer at a crossroads, in which he must choose.

Creative Directors: Joshua Breidenbach, Chí-An Benjamin De Leo & Gregory Jewett
Designer: Hélio Teles

www.slanted.de

J1059127351.title: Be Water
J1059127351.content:
016

Be Water
Poster 

Rice Studios
2020















Celebrate Bruce Lee’s story—as portrayed through the lens of director Bao Nguyen in the film “Be Water”. “Be Water” premiered over the summer of 2020, and to mark the occasion of what would have been Lee’s 80th birthday in late November, Ho Chi Minh City-based studio Rice was invited by director Bao Nguyen to created a series posters celebrating Bruce Lee and the film. The design aims to create a sense of tension by using contrasting and opposing ideas—both visually and culturally. A contrast between the iconic aesthetic of Enter the Dragon and a candid photo of Bruce Lee; the contrast between movie icon, and the individual.

Creative Directors: Joshua Breidenbach, Chí-An Benjamin De Leo & Gregory Jewett
Design: Hélio Teles

018

Good Intentions
Print

Whitman Emorson
2019















“Good Intentions” to kick-off a year of partnerships and opportunities. Good Intentions was a studio initiative of Whitman Emorson. The project consisted of a set of cards to thank clients and collaborators. The concept is a play on the saying “The road to hell is paved with good intentions”, meant to break with conservative norms.

R0605990576.title: Tomorrow Is Too Late
R0605990576.content:
020

Tomorrow Is Too Late
Editorial

Goods & Services
2018















The 1980s. On the upside: big hair, bright colours. On the downside: the Cold War, double-digit unemployment. In Toronto—and across North America and Europe—a punk rock scene known as “hardcore” emerged as a fast, vibrant voice of protest. Thirty years on, a handful of hardcore veterans began to dream of documenting that scene. Enlisted by the book’s authors, Derek Emerson and Shawn Chirrey, the project focused on copyediting and designing the publication while keeping the era’s DIY spirit alive within a sophisticated design and professional format. The result, Tomorrow Is Too Late, is packed with more than 300 pages of rare photographs, original flyers and raw memories from the people who were part of the scene.

Creative Directors: Carey George & Sue McCluskey
Art Directors: Nic Bradford & Taylor Toth
Designers: Sarah Rafter, Hélio Teles & Kristine Planche
Editors: Mike Barber, Michael Kanert & Erinn Steringa
Project Manager: Jess Arnold
Project Images: Taylor Toth

E2469039661.title: Grand Junction Park
E2469039661.content:
023

Grand Junction Park
Visual Identity

Bruce Mau Design
2015















Grand Junction Park is a new, all seasons, multifunctional development proposed by the City of Westfield, Indiana. The challenge was to create an inclusive and engaging visual identity, bringing all the neighbourhoods of the municipality around the park and its activities. Community involvement was key in developing the brand strategy and positioning. Interviews and workshops were conducted to get insights into the community’s expectations of the project. A playful graphic system was designed to enhance the democratic value of the park and its activities, the iconography at its core evolves and grows with the park.

Collaboration with Land Collective
Creative Directors: Elvira Barriga & Cristian Ordóñez
Designer: Hélio Teles
Architects: Fred Thwainy & Jordan Bischoff
Project Manager: Raylene Knutsen
Photography: Alan Karchmer

L3970727381.title: FAS
L3970727381.content:
024

Fundo de Arquitectura Social
Visual Identity

Freelance
2014















Fundo de Arquitectura Social (FAS), is a Lisbon-based collective for social architecture. The grassroots organization brings together community leaders, architects, sociologists and other professionals to develop initiatives to better different neighbourhoods of Lisbon. The challenge was to develop a brand identity that embodies the DIY nature of the organization while engaging community members in the creation of communication materials. A simple and flexible identity was designed, so that the community can create, produce and distribute on brand materials.

Design: Hélio Teles

I0550052919.title: Assay
I0550052919.content:
025

Assay Research 
Visual Identity

Freelance
2011















Assay PTDC/AAC — AMB/113649/2009, a research group composed by one Portuguese and two US universities, studies the fate and effects of silver nanoparticles in aquatic systems. The objective was to create a visual identity that reflects the subject's specificity while conveying information in an objective and effective manner. The approach devised is a graphic system that allows for fluid and mutable visual communications, similar to that of a nanoparticle.

Designer: Hélio Teles

H1112710106.title: Above View Below
H1112710106.content:
022

Above View Below
Poster

Freelance
2016















Poster for Above View Below, a VR documentary by Marie-Espérance Cerdà. In Above View Below, a virtual reality documentary, users follow @elusive.mind through roof hatches to the tallest views of downtown Toronto and down dark sewer tunnels. The challenge was to create an evocative visual system for promotional materials, such as posters and social media content. Original imagery as created based on the experiences pictured in the film.

Collaboration with Marie-Espérance Cerda
Design: Hélio Teles

F3761561114.title: CTY
F3761561114.content:
012

CTY Kitchen + Bar
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2021















CTY is a staple, all-day kitchen and bar at the core of one of HCMC’s most vibrant business towers. The name CTY has a twofold meaning: City and Công Ty, meaning company/corporation in Vietnamese. The identity is presented as a kit of independent parts to create a dynamic visual system that morphs and adapts to the space and its different activities and moments of the day.

Z4166887807.title: Nemesis
Z4166887807.content:
021

Nemesis Coffee
Visual Identity

Bruce Mau Design
2016















Design proposal for Nemesis, a coffee shop at the hearth of Vancouver’s West Hastings Street. The challenge was to create a visual identity under the owner’s philosophy of “coffee creating culture”, the idea of the brand being a window for the expression of the marginalized cultural currents. Building on the chosen name of Nemesis and the predefined icon of an inverted heart, a custom typeface was designed to unify the two elements under a cohesive whole. Its brut and unrefined style expresses the strength and the pride of the subcultures.

Creative Director: Cristian Ordóñez
Designer: Hélio Teles
Project Manager: Diana Kelly

Y2054987798.title: Rice Store
Y2054987798.content:
014

Rice Store
Visual Identity

Rice Studios
2020















Rice Store is a platform to expand upon the studio’s mission to broadcast extraordinaries stories through creativity, design and branding. At the intersection of thinking and making, rice store leverages on the studio’s skills in strategy, story telling, design and production to amplify voices behind creative endeavours in Vietnam and beyond. Rice Store exists online with occasional pop-ups around the world, bringing design from Vietnam further afield. The first pop-up occurred at PARCO Shibuya in Tokyo, Japan.

Creative Director: Joshua Breidenbach
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Designer: Lim Nuel
Architect: Aprar Elawad

U1822598657.title: Whitman Emorson
U1822598657.content:
019

Whitman Emorson
Visual Identity

Whitman Emorson
2018















Whitman Emorson is a Toronto-based design studio, aiming at solving complex problems with a human touch. The goal of the rebrand was to celebrate a decade long of existence and solidify the studio’s brand across channels. The solution was a custom wordmark to be used as a masthead, grounding the studio’s presence while creating a canvas for expression.

Creative Directors: Whitney Geller & Yasemin Emory
Design Director: Hélio Teles
Designer: Jade Courroy
